title: Chocolate and hazelnut cookies
subtitle: soft, chewy cookies packed with dark chocolate chips and toasted hazelnuts
excerpt: Chocolate and hazelnut cookies are large, soft-centred drop cookies with dark chocolate chips and roughly chopped toasted hazelnuts folded through the dough. The dough is chilled before baking so the cookies hold their shape and stay thick rather than spreading flat. They come out of the oven soft in the centre and firm at the edges.
sourceNotes: Chocolate chip cookies in the American tradition were developed in the late 1930s by Ruth Wakefield at the Toll House Inn, Massachusetts. The combination with hazelnuts became a popular variation in American and British home baking, drawing on the classic Italian pairing of hazelnuts and chocolate in gianduja.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the shaped, unbaked dough balls. Bake from frozen at 180 degrees C, adding 3 to 4 minutes to the baking time.
recipe.batchNotes: The dough freezes well so it is worth making a double batch.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough keeps refrigerated for up to 3 days. Bake as needed.

content.text: Chocolate and hazelnut cookies are large, soft-centred drop cookies made from a buttery brown sugar dough with dark chocolate chips and chopped toasted hazelnuts. Chilling the dough before baking prevents excessive spreading and gives the cookies a thick, chewy centre. They look underdone when they come out of the oven but set up firm on the tray as they cool.

items.prepNote: 70 per cent, roughly chopped into chips
toasted, skins rubbed off, roughly chopped

content.text: Beat the softened butter with both sugars until light and creamy, about 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs and vanilla extract.
Sift in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, and salt. Mix until just combined. Fold in the chocolate and hazelnuts.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. The dough will firm significantly.

Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Line baking trays with baking paper. Scoop the dough into rounds about 50 g each and place on the trays, spaced 6 cm apart. Do not press down.

Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until the edges are set and pale golden but the centres still look soft and slightly underdone. Leave on the tray for 5 minutes before transferring to a rack; the cookies firm up as they cool.

attrs.problem: Cookies spreading too flat and thin
attrs.avoid: Avoid skipping the chilling step or using warm dough from a warm kitchen.
attrs.fix: Refrigerate the dough for the full hour. If the cookies still spread, chill the shaped dough balls on the tray for 15 minutes before baking.

attrs.problem: Cookies hard all the way through instead of soft in the centre
attrs.avoid: Avoid overbaking; the cookies continue to cook on the tray after they come out of the oven.
attrs.fix: Take them out when the edges are just set and the centres still look a little underdone. They will be perfectly set after 5 minutes resting on the hot tray.
